**Midtklyngen** is a healthcare cluster (*sundhedsklynge*) operating within [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] [^src6]. It is one of the local organizational units systematically evaluated in the Danish national quality reports for [[atrieflimren]] (AFDK), published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) [^src1]. The cluster is frequently highlighted in these reports for its clinical performance, treatment coverage, and adherence to national standards.

In the 2024 AFDK report, Midtklyngen meets the national standard for Indikator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy, achieving a result of 92.9% [^src1]. Regarding [[indikator-4a]] (treatment coverage), the 2024 report notes that Midtklyngen is the only cluster where patients meet the standard, with 58% of patients residing in the cluster fulfilling the requirement [^src5]. The subsequent 2025 report further emphasizes this success, stating that Midtklyngen is the only healthcare cluster where patients meet the development target for [[indikator-4a]], reaching a proportion of 62% [^src11]. Additionally, Midtklyngen fulfills the standard for [[indikator-4b]] within Region Midtjylland [^src4].

In terms of clinical outcomes and geographic distribution, Midtklyngen is included in national mapping for [[indikator-5]], which tracks the incidence of ischemic stroke (apoplexy) among patients with atrial fibrillation [^src4]. Other clusters evaluated alongside Midtklyngen in these regional comparisons include [[aarhusklyngen]], [[randersklyngen]], [[horsensklyngen]], and [[goedstrupklyngen]] [^src4].

Most notably, Midtklyngen demonstrates exceptional performance in patient education. For [[indikator-8]], which tracks the provision of structured patient education within the first year of an atrial fibrillation diagnosis, Midtklyngen is the only healthcare cluster to meet the national target of ≥ 50% in the 2023/24 measurement period. It achieved a rate of 62.1% (95% CI: 58.8–65.3), significantly outperforming other regions and clusters that struggled with systemic implementation barriers [^src10].
